Left and right are confirmed blocked by adjacent mirror walls (evidenced by large, partially off-screen close self-reflections at the view edges). The only traversable path is forward south out of the starting alcove/corridor segment; the central self-reflection comes from a mirror further past the next open cell, so this forward move will not cause a collision.

North, east, and south are confirmed blocked by adjacent mirror walls (south verified via collision, others by close full-field self-reflections). Turn right to face the only open west direction, then move forward out of the starting alcove into the open adjacent corridor cell.

East, South, and West sides of the starting cell are confirmed blocked (South/West via forward collisions, East via close adjacent mirror wall reflection). A fully enclosed cell is impossible, so turn right to face the only open north exit, then move forward out of the starting alcove.

North is blocked by an immediate mirror wall (large close front self-reflection). Turn left to face west (the only open traversable direction along the corridor), then move forward one cell west to progress.

West (front) and North (right) are blocked by adjacent mirror walls (evidenced by close life-size self-reflections); East is the return path from the previous cell. Turn left to face the open South direction, then move forward one cell South to continue exploring the maze without unnecessary collision.

This cell is a dead end with walls blocking south, east, and west, no beacon present. Turn 180 degrees right to face the open north exit, then move forward to return to the east-west corridor to continue exploration, with no expected collisions.

Return south to cell C (where an open west corridor was previously overlooked), turn west to face the confirmed open purple-tiled corridor, and move one cell west into new unexplored territory with no expected collisions.

Traverse two cells west along the straight, mirror-lined corridor. The small apparent size of the nearest front self-reflection confirms no blocking walls exist between current position and the second cell ahead, allowing collision-free progress while minimizing planning steps.

Front and left are blocked by adjacent mirror walls (evidenced by the close full front self-reflection and close left side self-reflection); back is the return path we came from. Move two cells west along the straight continuous mirror corridor. The small apparent size of the front self-reflection confirms no blocking walls for two steps ahead, and evenly spaced support poles verify no side turns, allowing collision-free progress into unexplored territory.

Turn right to face the open west exit of this dead-end east alcove, then move forward west to return to the prior junction cell to continue exploration with no expected collision.
